Priority will also be given to small businesses affected by natural disasters, marginalised communities in coastal and haor regions, differently abled individuals and returning migrant workers.
Student banking account holders aged up to 25 can access concessional loans to finance vocational training, income-generating activities and higher education expenses, subject to guarantees from their guardians.

Bangladesh Bank sells $205m to banks, dollar rate falls below Tk125
12 November, 2026, 11:40 pm
Following the auction, remittance houses lowered their dollar selling rates to below Tk125, from Tk125.30-Tk125.40 earlier in the day, easing pressure on the exchange rate.
12 November, 2026, 11:40 pm
Bangladesh Bank sold $205 million from its foreign exchange reserves to commercial banks through an auction today (12 November), bringing down the dollar rate offered by remittance houses to below Tk125.
The central bank sold the dollars at Tk124.74 each and instructed participating banks not to resell the purchased dollars in the interbank market, warning that such transactions could disrupt the foreign exchange market.
Earlier this month, Bangladesh Bank sold $120 million at Tk124.30-Tk124.35 per dollar.
After selling the dollar, the reserve position stood at $29.82 billion, down from $30.12 billion yesterday. Arief Hossain Khan, spokesperson for the central bank, has confirmed the matter.
A senior commercial bank official said remittance houses had offered dollars to banks at Tk125.30-Tk125.40 this morning, with some banks purchasing them at Tk125.30-Tk125.32.
However, following the central bank's auction, several commercial banks bought dollars at Tk124.90-Tk124.95, while some secured rates below Tk124.90.
Another senior banker said remittance houses began offering dollars below Tk125 after Bangladesh Bank released $205 million into the market, helping ease exchange rate pressure. However, he said the central bank should plan such interventions more prudently.
He noted that the central bank issued the auction notice at 1:20pm. Had it been announced in the morning, the dollar rate could have fallen further, particularly as demand for foreign currency is generally higher at the beginning of the month. Banks also need time to arrange funds to buy dollars, he added.
Another commercial bank official said banks had purchased more than $300 million from remittance houses today, partly because rising fuel prices had increased import costs and the amount of foreign currency needed to pay for oil imports.
A senior banker said $205 million is a substantial amount and argued that releasing a similar volume several days earlier could have prevented the dollar rate from crossing Tk125. He also called for the central bank to analyse how much foreign currency should be released to help stabilise the market.

14 November, 2026, 09:40 pm
The country's leading pharmaceutical companies managed to sustain revenue and profit growth in the July-September quarter of FY27 despite disruptions in gas and electricity supplies and rising fuel costs, although their expansion slowed to mostly single-digit rates.
Among the listed drug makers that disclosed quarterly results, Square Pharmaceuticals, Beximco Pharmaceuticals, Renata, Beacon Pharmaceuticals, Acme Laboratories and IBN Sina Pharmaceuticals reported increases in both revenue and profit. However, ACI and Silva Pharmaceuticals incurred losses, while Advent and Navana Pharmaceuticals saw their profits decline.
Square Pharma remained the largest listed drug maker by revenue and profit, reporting consolidated revenue of Tk2,244 crore, up 4% year-on-year, and net profit of Tk777 crore, a 5% increase. Beximco Pharma posted revenue of Tk1,466 crore, up 6%, while its profit rose 8% to Tk260 crore.
Renata recorded 11% revenue growth to Tk1,260 crore, while its profit jumped 38% to Tk102 crore. The company attributed the improvement mainly to higher revenue and lower net finance expenses, reflecting the impact of capital restructuring and prudent management of foreign exchange and interest rate risks.
Beacon Pharma delivered the fastest revenue growth among the major players, with turnover rising 13% to Tk463 crore. Its profit increased 50% to Tk78 crore. Acme Laboratories reported 11% revenue growth to Tk1,101 crore and a 13% rise in profit to Tk72 crore. IBN Sina's revenue and profit grew 7% and 9% to Tk398 crore and Tk24 crore, respectively.
Beximco Pharma Managing Director SM Rabbur Reza, in a statement to the London Stock Exchange, where the company's global depository receipts are listed, said the results demonstrated the underlying strength and resilience of its business despite ongoing macroeconomic challenges.
He said the company had continued to deliver revenue and profitability growth while pursuing its strategy of supplying affordable medicines at home and abroad.
A senior researcher at an asset management company said the sector had faced significant pressure from gas and electricity shortages, while higher fuel prices had added to inflation and operating costs.
Even the leading companies, which traditionally delivered double-digit growth, have reported mostly single-digit expansion in revenue and profit this time, he said. However, the pharmaceutical sector has performed relatively well compared with many other industries amid the severe external shocks. Smaller and weaker companies have been more exposed to the pressure.
The results show a widening gap between companies with stronger operating capacity and those struggling to absorb higher costs. ACI reported consolidated revenue growth of 12% to Tk4,149 crore, but swung to a loss of Tk18.84 crore from a profit of Tk3.40 crore a year earlier, mainly due to higher finance costs against debt. 'No work, no pay': RMG factory owners threaten closures from tomorrow amid labour unrest
14 November, 2026, 04:10 pm
Garment factory owners are set to shut unrest-hit units indefinitely from tomorrow (15 November) under the Labour Act if workers do not return to work, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) has said.
The closures will be made under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006. In this context, under Section 13(1), a factory may be shut down indefinitely if it is forced to suspend production due to labour unrest. Workers will not be entitled to wages for the period during which the factory remains closed.
Speaking at a press conference today (14 November), BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan said owners of factories in the affected areas are in a difficult situation and cannot keep their factories running.
He also said these owners have told the association they will be compelled to close their factories under the section.
Fifty-five factories have already been declared closed under the section today, he said. Another 147 factories suspended production today as workers did not work.
The BGMEA president did not say how many factories would be closed under Section 13(1) from tomorrow. He said unrest does not occur in the same factories every day, so the number may change.
The 147 factories that stopped production today employ around 3 lakh workers, he added.
Leaders of BGMEA and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) were present at the press conference.

14 November, 2026, 07:50 pm
The country’s energy sector received $2.54 billion in climate finance between 2002 and 2023, but 92% came as loans and 18.84% of designated funding went to fossil-fuel projects, the index findings show.
14 November, 2026, 07:50 pm
Bangladesh has an estimated climate debt of $80 per person, placing it in the "High Risk" category of a new global index, according to findings presented at a policy dialogue at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, today (14 November).
Dhaka-based think tanks Change Initiative and Young Power in Social Action (YPSA) organised the dialogue titled "25 Years of Climate Finance: Progress, Gaps and Transformative Solutions."
Data presented at the session showed that 92% of the $2.54 billion in climate finance directed to Bangladesh's energy sector between 2002 and 2023 came as loans. Moreover, 18.84% of the funding designated for climate projects went to fossil-fuel initiatives.
Speaking at the dialogue, Barrister Mahbubul Alam Salehin, lawmaker for Kurigram-3, highlighted the human cost of climate change, saying families in riverine chars had been displaced and relocated up to 20 times.
"Bangladesh must not become poorer in the process of protecting itself from climate change," he said, questioning whether vulnerable communities receive tangible support before disasters and whether they must repay it.
69% of climate fund came as loan
Speakers criticised the global climate finance system for shifting the cost of climate recovery onto countries least responsible for emissions.
According to Change Initiative, 69% of public climate finance provided to developing countries in 2022 came as loans rather than grants. International public adaptation finance also fell from $28 billion in 2022 to $26 billion in 2023, with 58% delivered as debt.
"What we are observing right now in the name of climate finance is debt by design," said M Zakir Hossain Khan, co-founder and chief executive of Change Initiative, who chaired the dialogue.
Muhammad Haseeb Khan, project lead for West and South Asia at the Climate Vulnerable Forum and V20 Secretariat, said vulnerable economies borrowed at interest rates of 15-18%, compared with 2-3% for wealthy nations. They often had to repay infrastructure loans within three to four years, although the facilities were designed to last decades.
Seven of nine planetary boundaries breached
Researchers warned that tackling climate change separately from wider ecological damage was failing to protect the planet.
Seven of the nine planetary boundaries have now been breached, compared with three when the framework was first assessed in 2009. Only the ozone layer is recovering, which researchers attributed to a dedicated fund covering developing countries' transition costs.
Despite nature absorbing roughly half of human-caused carbon emissions, international biodiversity finance stood at just $18.9 billion in 2024, around one-sixth of the $115.9 billion mobilised for climate finance in 2022.
"We've been mobilising significant funds – not sufficient, but mobilising – yet we are still breaching the boundaries," said Mofazzal Hossain, research coordinator at Change Initiative.
Proposed alternatives to climate borrowing
Change Initiative proposed 12 non-debt revenue mechanisms that could generate $35 billion-$400 billion annually by the early 2030s, with a medium-case estimate of $160 billion.
Proposals include a climate damages tax on fossil fuel profits ($60 billion annually), a 2% minimum tax on billionaires ($25 billion), redirecting fossil fuel subsidies ($15 billion) and a 1% contribution from national military budgets ($15 billion).
Other proposed levies target premium air travel and private jets, carbon border adjustments, financial transactions, international shipping, plastics, cryptocurrency mining and AI data centres.

British Council honours 64 students at Scholars’ Award 2026
14 November, 2026, 07:50 pm
The British Council recognised 64 students from 30 English-medium schools across Bangladesh for their results in the May–June 2026 examination session at the Scholars' Award 2026 ceremony, held at Radisson Blu Dhaka Water Garden on 14 November.
More than 200 school leaders, educators, parents and representatives from the British Council's network of 200 partner schools attended the ceremony, according to the press release.
The awards recognised students who earned the highest distinction grades in nine or more subjects in Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel O Level, IGCSE and International GCSE examinations. The British Council administers these examinations on behalf of UK examination boards. Seven A Level students were also honoured.
City Bank PLC sponsored scholarships of Tk25,000 each for the 57 O Level, IGCSE and International GCSE awardees to support their future studies. The seven A Level awardees received gift vouchers from GoZayaan, the event's travel partner.
Maarya Rehman, deputy director of the British Council in Bangladesh, said the number of awardees had risen from 22 when the programme began to 64 this year, showing steady growth.
"That growth tells us something about the ambition of our young people and the strength of our partner schools," she said.
Rehman said the British Council aimed to administer examinations with integrity and connect students with international opportunities through its school network, underlining its wider role.
City Bank Deputy Managing Director and Head of Retail Banking Md Arup Haider said he hoped the awards would encourage students to realise their potential and contribute to Bangladesh's future. Farjana Absar Jeba, assistant manager for commercial operations at GoZayaan Limited, also urged the students to pursue their ambitions.
Zunayed Ahmed, managing director and head of market at British Council Bangladesh, said earning top grades in nine or more subjects reflected students' hard work, discipline and curiosity. He urged the awardees to keep learning and use their knowledge to make a difference in Bangladesh and abroad.
All 64 students received crests and certificates. One awardee spoke about their studies, the challenges they faced and their plans for the future. Tahnee Yeasmin, director of business development at British Council Bangladesh, delivered the vote of thanks.
Representatives of international examination boards also attended. They included Sarwat Reza and Md Nakib Haider from Cambridge University Press and Assessment, Abdullah Al Mamun and Jannatul Ferdous Sigma from Pearson Edexcel, and Shahin Reza of Oxford AQA.

Cenbank to ease expat bond rules, expand NRC accounts for forex
14 November, 2026, 07:20 pm
Bangladesh Bank is planning to attract more foreign currency through Non-Resident Convertible (NRC) accounts and ease investment and maturity restrictions on three types of expatriate bonds to strengthen the country's foreign exchange reserves, Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman has said.
He made the remarks at the fifth Bangladesh Economic Summit 2026, organised by Bonik Barta at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Dhaka today (14 November).
The governor said NRC accounts had already been introduced, and the central bank, with support from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), was conducting international promotional campaigns to encourage foreign currency deposits through the facility.
He expressed optimism that the initiative would help bolster the country's foreign exchange reserves.
Citing examples from neighbouring countries, Mostaqur Rahman said India had raised $32 billion through similar accounts within four to five months, while Pakistan had mobilised $13 billion.
Bangladesh also aims to attract foreign currency through the NRC account facility, he added.
The governor said the central bank was working to ensure that payments due under NRC accounts over the next three to four years did not exert significant pressure on the country's foreign exchange reserves.
The governor also announced plans to ease maturity and investment-related restrictions on three types of bonds available to expatriate Bangladeshis.
He said the maximum tenure of these bonds had been capped at 15 years around five years ago for unspecified reasons. The authorities were now working to make their maturity periods and investment opportunities more flexible.
Investments in the three types of bonds currently total the equivalent of $604 million, he said.
Mostaqur Rahman expressed hope that relaxing the restrictions would attract additional foreign currency, strengthen reserves and increase dollar supply in the domestic foreign exchange market.
He said the initiatives were intended to ease pressure on foreign exchange reserves while encouraging expatriate Bangladeshis to invest more in the country.

Idra favours closure of weak insurers, BIA seeks restructuring
14 November, 2026, 07:45 pm
The Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority (Idra) is considering shutting down financially unsound insurance companies that lack the capacity to operate, while the Bangladesh Insurance Association (BIA) has called for restructuring troubled insurers instead of closing them outright.
Idra Chairman Mir Nadia Nivin said the regulator will take legal action against companies that fail to meet financial requirements and, if necessary, shut down both life and non-life insurers through due legal procedures.
She made the remarks at a roundtable titled "Towards a Stronger and Sustainable Insurance Industry: The Way Forward" at Professor Dr Abdullah Faruk Multipurpose Hall of the Faculty of Business Studies at the University of Dhaka yesterday.
Financial strength and solvency under scrutiny
Nivin said Bangladesh has 82 insurance companies, but their financial strength and operational conditions vary considerably. The regulator needs to identify which companies are financially sound and which lack the capacity to meet their liabilities, she said.
Insurers that fail to meet solvency requirements should not be allowed to continue operating, she added. Depending on their financial condition, the regulator could also restrict their business activities and product offerings.
Such assessments should be based on internationally accepted and reliable actuarial evaluations rather than figures presented in companies' financial statements, she said.
The Idra chairman also said the Insurance Act 2010 has become outdated in view of developments in the financial sector. Significant amendments are being considered to modernise the law and strengthen its enforcement, she said.
Companies that have failed to operate properly will face action in accordance with legal procedures, she added.

BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan has alleged that an anarchic situation is being created to pave the way for an irrational wage announcement.
The BGMEA President said, “The wage board was formed on 1 November. The chaotic situation began in the last week of October. If we consider what happened last month as logical, then what is happening now is not logical at all. The wage board has already been formed.”
He further stated, “The most crucial matter—when the increased wages will be effective—was announced at the very first meeting of the board. Despite this, creating an anarchic situation means setting the stage for an irrational wage announcement under pressure.”
BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan said these things in response to a journalist's question at a joint press briefing of the two organisations of garment industry owners—BGMEA and BKMEA.
The press conference held at the BGMEA complex in Uttara on Saturday afternoon was attended by BKMEA Executive President Fazle Shamim Ehsan, Vice President Amal Poddar, BGMEA Vice President Rezwan Selim, Mizanur Rahman, among others.
Referring to the ongoing unrest, BGMEA President, in a written statement, mentioned that 147 factories in Savar-Ashulia and Gazipur are unable to continue production activities despite efforts, due to the disruption in overall security and favourable production environment. If the factories fail to carry out production activities due to ongoing labour unrest, they will be forced to close from tomorrow under Section 13 (1) of the labour law.
The BGMEA President said that 55 factories in Savar-Ashulia and Gazipur were closed indefinitely under Section 13 (1) today, Saturday.
However, 92 factories tried but failed to resume production. These factories were compelled to grant leave.
In response to a question, the BGMEA President said, “According to labour law, there is no provision to close factories under Section 13 (1) whose operations are ongoing and can conduct regular production. However, those unable to do so, wherever they might be, have that right.”

RMG owners announce closure from tomorrow if workers do not report for work
Published: 14 Nov 2026, 10: 59
Garment workers who do not report to work will lead factory owners to close their factories starting tomorrow, Sunday, according to Article 13(1) of the Labour Law.
Under this article, workers do not receive payment when factories are closed. In other words, no work means no pay.
Today, Saturday, Mahmud Hasan Khan, the president of the garment industry owners' organization BGMEA, stated this at a press conference.
BGMEA, along with BKMEA, organised this press conference at the BGMEA office in Uttara, Dhaka.
Earlier in the morning, over a thousand garment factory owners participated in a joint meeting of the two organisations.
The BGMEA president stated that 55 factories in Savar, Ashulia, and Gazipur are closed indefinitely under Article 13(1) of the Labour Law.
Additionally, 92 factories halted production due to worker protests. From tomorrow, those factories that cannot resume production may choose to remain closed under Article 13(1).
Mahmud Hasan Khan further mentioned that the owners will present their proposal at the Wage Board meeting on the upcoming Monday. However, if the chaos continues, a decision will be made on whether to participate in the board’s discussion.
Meanwhile, during a joint press conference of five workers' organisations held yesterday, Friday, a call was made for workers to maintain patience and restraint.
Worker leaders stated that the Wage Board's process to determine fair wages is in progress. Workers should not engage in any activities that might disrupt this process and should abstain from provocation and misdeeds. They urged workers to return to work to allow the Wage Board the opportunity for discussion.
Addressing the owners, labour leaders said that currently, movements are ongoing in a few places. The path to resolving these issues through dialogue should remain open.
Garment workers have been protesting since last month demanding a wage increase. On 1 November, the government formed a minimum wage board.
During the Wage Board's second meeting last Monday, the workers' representative proposed a minimum wage of Tk 32,000.
The third meeting of the board is scheduled for this coming Monday. Since the commencement of the Wage Board discussions, there has been some improvement in the industrial area's situation, although it has not completely stabilised.

AI training free of charge with Tk 200 daily allowance: HSC pass students can apply
Published: 14 Nov 2026, 08: 32
The government will provide free basic training in artificial intelligence (AI) technology to young people across all 64 districts of the country to help them develop relevant skills.
The Department of Youth Development has arranged a two-month training programme for this purpose. Young people aged between 18 and 35 can apply.
The Department of Youth Development has announced that interested candidates must submit their applications by 11:59 pm on 24 November.
The training will take place under the project titled “Skills Development of IT-Literate Youth through Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technology”, implemented by the Department of Youth Development under the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
According to the relevant notice, the third batch of the “Basic Training Course on Artificial Intelligence (AI)” will run from 1 December to 31 January 2027. Participants will receive six hours of training each day, completing a total of 300 hours over 50 days.
Applicants must have passed at least the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) or an equivalent examination. They must also have basic knowledge of computers and information technology. During the selection process, the authorities will give preference to candidates with basic computer and ICT knowledge and proficiency in English.
Interested candidates can apply through Department of Youth Development AI Project portal. The application link will close automatically after the deadline. Applicants must download and retain a copy of their application form after submission. The authorities will notify eligible applicants of the examination date, time and venue through SMS.
Important admission dates
28 November: Written examination
29 November: Viva voce
30 November: Publication of the final list of selected trainees
Applicants do not have to pay any admission fees for the training programme. In addition, non-residential trainees will receive a daily travel allowance of Tk 200.
The authorities will also provide meals every day during the training period. Participants who successfully complete the course and fulfil the prescribed requirements will receive certificates.
The authorities have divided the training programme into four regional packages.
Under Package 1, E-Learning and Earning Ltd will conduct training in 17 districts across the Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions.
Under Package 2, a joint venture comprising SEO Expert Bangladesh Ltd, European IT Solution Institute and Kaizen IT will conduct training in 16 districts across the Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions.
Under Package 3, E-Learning and Earning Ltd will conduct training in 16 districts across the Barishal and Khulna divisions.
Meanwhile, under Package 4, a joint venture comprising Service Engines Ltd, Dot Com Systems Ltd and Wizard Software Technology Bangladesh will conduct training in 15 districts across the Chattogram and Sylhet divisions.

Tk 567.5b govt projects to bring healthcare to people's doorsteps
Published: 13 Nov 2026, 11: 45
The government has moved to implement two major health-sector projects involving a proposed investment of Tk 567.5064 billion to expand treatment capacity at upazila health complexes and strengthen primary healthcare infrastructure at union and ward levels across the country.
The projects, scheduled to be implemented between December 2026 and November 2029, aim to construct, reconstruct, upgrade, remodel and renovate healthcare facilities, expand treatment capacity and improve access to essential services, particularly for rural and marginalised communities.
According to the draft Development Project Proposal (DPP) received from the Planning Commission, the first project, titled 'Construction, Reconstruction, Upgradation, Remodeling and Repair and Reform Works of Health Complexes at Upazila Level in Bangladesh', has a proposed cost of Tk 447.57385 billion.
The second, titled 'Construction, Reconstruction, Upgradation, Remodeling and Repair and Reform Works of Health Infrastructures at Union and Ward Level in Bangladesh', involves Tk 119.932582 billion.
Both projects propose full government financing. The Planning Commission has recommended further scrutiny of implementation arrangements, construction costs, procurement plans, staffing requirements and environmental safeguards before approval.
Talking to BSS, State Minister for Health and Family Welfare M A Muhit said the present government has inherited a health system suffering from inadequate infrastructure, equipment and manpower, while many facilities at union and upazila levels had remained unrepaired or unrenovated for years.
Existing 30-bed and 50-bed upazila health complexes are no longer adequate for many areas, where populations have grown substantially, with some upazilas now serving eight to 10 lakh people, he said.
As part of a major initiative to rebuild the health sector, the government has taken a "historic" decision to transform health complexes in all 503 upazilas into fully equipped 151-bed hospitals, he added.
The government is also rebuilding and renovating union-level healthcare facilities, making primary healthcare the centrepiece of its broader reform programme. The objective is to enable upazila hospitals to treat around 80 percent of common and moderately complex illnesses, including maternal and child health conditions, reducing pressure on district and divisional hospitals.
Upazila hospitals to receive major infrastructure upgrades
According to project documents, the proposed Tk 447.57385 billion project will be implemented by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) while the Public Works Department and Health Engineering Department will execute construction works.
The project targets include 18 hospitals with 51 beds each, 305 with 101 beds, 83 with 132 beds, 13 with 120 beds and 24 with 151 beds each. It also includes integrated multi-storey service buildings at 443 upazilas and residential facilities for doctors, nurses and other staff at 15 upazilas.
It will replace unsafe buildings, retrofit structurally suitable facilities and renovate existing infrastructure. It also covers internal roads, boundary walls, gates, guardrooms, water supply, drainage and electricity networks.
The upgraded hospitals will have intensive care units, coronary care units, one-stop emergency centres, modern operation theatres, maternal and newborn care, kidney dialysis, eye treatment, cancer screening and separate physiotherapy services for male and female patients.
The project also envisages central medical gas supplies, medical waste management, sewage treatment plants, fire safety systems, solar power and backup generators. Improved infrastructure and treatment capacity are also expected to help reduce maternal and infant mortality.

India blocks over 100 speakers from opposition democracy summit
Updated: 13 Nov 2026, 11: 08
Bharat Summit X handle Bharat Summit
India blocked more than 100 international speakers from attending a democracy summit organised by the opposition Congress party, a senior opposition politician said on Friday.
Those denied visas included a Norwegian journalist who had previously questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi about press freedom.
Shashi Tharoor, a Congress MP and former senior United Nations official, said 115 of the 315 speakers cleared by India’s foreign ministry were subsequently refused entry or had their visas cancelled, “apparently on the instructions” of the home ministry.
“It is completely unclear under what provision of law the government has taken such a drastic step,” Tharoor wrote on X.
“What a shame that a proud democracy has become so insecure that it must stifle any voices it fears will be critical!” he added.
Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng said on Wednesday that her visa was cancelled shortly before she was due to travel to India, where she had been invited to speak on media and press freedom.
She had questioned Modi at a press briefing during his visit to Oslo in May.
The Editors Guild of India condemned the cancellation and said the move smacked of “bureaucratic overreach” and called on the government to disclose its reasons and reverse the decision.
The two-day summit, which opened on Friday in the city of Hyderabad, brings together around 1,000 delegates from more than 70 countries to discuss democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and global cooperation.
India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

Microsoft outage: Word 365, Outlook, Teams unavailable in Bangladesh
Published: 13 Nov 2026, 09: 48
Microsoft, Teams, Outlook and Copilot logos are seen in this illustration taken on 13 November 2026. Reuters
Microsoft has been hit by a major technical outage worldwide since 11:32 pm on Thursday (Bangladesh time).
The outage, which has lasted more than 14 hours, has left millions of people across the world, including Bangladesh, unable to use Microsoft's email service Outlook, video conferencing software Microsoft Teams and Word 365 online. As a result, various organisations are facing major disruptions.
Users of Outlook email services at several corporate organisations in Bangladesh have been unable to access the service since morning.
Global Microsoft outage: steps to fix not going 'as expected'
13 Nov 2026
Mostafizur Rahman, an official at a research organisation who did not wish to disclose the name of his institution, said, “We have been unable to use Microsoft Outlook since last night. Although our office is closed today, Friday, all our work online has come to a halt.”
According to Downdetector, a website that monitors website outages, major disruptions to Microsoft services had spread to 74 countries within approximately an hour of the worldwide outage beginning. Various Microsoft services are still unavailable worldwide.
News agency Reuters reports: A disruption of Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot stretched into Asia-Pacific business hours on Friday after affecting thousands of US users, as the tech giant struggled to fix server problems it blamed for the outage.
The outage hit government agencies in Australia, Japan and the United States, as well as companies including OpenAI and Anthropic. It is the second disruption to Microsoft's 365 services this year, raising concerns that repeated failures could push corporate clients to question Microsoft's reliability.
Downdetector, which tracks outages by collating status reports from a number ⁠of sources, showed more than 18,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US at 11:30 p.m. ET (0430 GMT). It also showed outages for several Microsoft services in the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia and Japan, early Friday local time.
At its peak, Downdetector showed more than 130,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US around 1 p.m. ET on Thursday. The outage has lasted for about 12 hours.
In a service health notice, Microsoft said features of Microsoft 365 services that depended on Exchange Online and email were affected, while elements that did not rely on Exchange Online remained functional. Exchange Online is the company's cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks.
US AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic said they had faced issues with Microsoft connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email support services were impacted.
Microsoft faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year ⁠and also in October last year.
The tech giant last month also reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide, according to Reuters.

Published: 13 Nov 2026, 07: 10
Cancer-stricken daughter of Jobel Mia and Salma Begum at Mosabbir Memorial Alok Nibash in the Bashundhara Residential Area, Takia Mansura Hossain
At the age of two and a half, Shraddha Biswas was diagnosed with blood cancer. She is now five years old. Her parents, Rupa Rani and Bandhan Biswas, from Jashore, have been fighting a long and difficult battle to ensure treatment for their only child. It took considerable time to diagnose the disease, and the expenses were enormous. They came to Dhaka and began treatment at the National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital in Mohakhali. They rented a house near the hospital at Tk 200 per day, in addition to the cost of food.
One day, Rupa Rani noticed an address on a piece of paper posted on a hospital wall. The address was ‘Mosabbir Memorial Alok Nibash’ in the Bashundhara Residential Area.
Now, for the past two years, the parents have been staying at Alok Nibash whenever they come to Dhaka with their daughter for treatment. They do not have to pay anything for accommodation or meals. Nurses at the residence also monitor whether the child is taking her medication properly. The family receives counselling services as well. An ambulance service is available to transport patients between the residence and the National Cancer Institute. All these services are provided free of charge.
Cancer patients can stay free of charge at Mosabbir Memorial Alok Nibash in the Bashundhara Residential Area Mansura Hossain
On the afternoon of 8 November, I spoke with Rupa Rani at the six-storey Alok Nibash. Shraddha was in a bit of a bad mood. She refused to leave her mother's lap and did not want to talk. Her mother had done her hair up with several clips.
Rupa Rani said that Shraddha's father works as a security guard at a private company, and the family lives in Jashore. There are hardly any facilities for treating childhood blood cancer there. A local doctor had initially told them that their daughter had thalassemia. However, after coming to Dhaka, they learned that she had cancer.
She said the cost of treatment was very high. Had they not found out about this residence, it would have been impossible for them to afford their daughter's treatment in Dhaka, along with accommodation and food expenses.
Even when her husband cannot come to Dhaka regularly, it does not create any difficulties. The residence takes care of all the necessary arrangements.

Published: 13 Nov 2026, 06: 01
Bangladesh Bank File Photo
Looking to start a business but lacking capital? Securing a bank loan typically requires collateral. Also, small entrepreneurs and low-income professionals often fail to qualify because they lack the necessary documents and financial capacity.
Bangladesh Bank has set up a Tk 15 billion refinancing fund to bring small entrepreneurs, low-income professionals and other marginalised groups without collateral or adequate financial documents under the formal banking system.
Under the scheme, banks will receive refinancing facilities from the central bank at an annual interest rate of 1 per cent and lend to customers at a maximum rate of 7 per cent.
Individuals can borrow up to Tk 10 lakh, while group loans can go up to Tk 40 lakh. No collateral will be required for loans of up to Tk 5 lakh. The loan tenure will be five years.
The Financial Inclusion Department of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular on Thursday outlining the scheme.
According to the circular, farmers, small traders, low-income professionals, women entrepreneurs, students, members of expatriate families and people affected by disasters will receive priority. Persons with disabilities and members of the third gender will also be eligible. At least 25 per cent of the total loan disbursement under the fund must be allocated to women.
The directive, sent to the managing directors and chief executive officers of all scheduled banks, sets out the eligibility criteria, loan amounts, interest rates, collateral requirements and disbursement procedures.
Bangladesh Bank said the initiative aims to improve the living standards of marginalised and disadvantaged groups by involving them in income-generating activities and expanding financial inclusion. A new policy has been formulated for the scheme.
Who will be eligible for the loans
Priority will be given to micro and small entrepreneurs operating in neighbourhoods, local communities and villages. Eligible occupations include fishermen, cobblers, goldsmiths, hawkers, blacksmiths, potters, tailors, rickshaw and van drivers, carpenters, masons, painters and plumbers. People involved in repairing electrical and electronic appliances, making pickles and traditional cakes, as well as small-scale weavers and tea workers, will also be eligible.
Grocery and general store owners, mobile clothing vendors, mobile recharge and mobile financial service agents, information and internet service providers, street food vendors, tea and betel leaf sellers, book and newspaper vendors, flower, fruit and vegetable sellers, and people rearing poultry and livestock can also apply.
Beyond traditional businesses, the scheme will cover people involved in freelancing, nursery businesses, tree planting, embroidery, block printing and batik, cottage industries, handicrafts, food production and promising innovative ventures. Trained members of the Village Defence Party (VDP) will also be eligible for loans to undertake various income-generating activities.

COP31: Climate governance must be built on justice
Published: 13 Nov 2026, 04: 45
A woman sits at the Iranian pavilion designed in memory of children killed in the Minab school strike, during the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, 11 November 2026. Reuters
I do not know whether world leaders visited the Iran Pavilion during the Leaders’ Summit of the climate conference in Turkiye. Children wearing flower garlands around their necks are welcoming everyone there with smiling faces. Beside them are the remains of a damaged schoolroom, a burnt schoolbag, a favourite doll hanging from the bag’s zipper, and a broken blackboard in front of them. There are no mathematics problems, grammar lessons or homework written on the board. Instead, the words written in chalk read: 168 children killed in Israeli and US attacks.
On the very first day of the unjust US-Israeli war against Iran, which began on 28 February, these children were killed in an attack on the Shajareh Tayyebeh girls’ elementary school in Minab, in the country’s south. These children have lost their names and identities and have become mere ‘numbers’.
The number 168, written on the blackboard as part of the installation depicting the horrific consequences of war at the Iran Pavilion, left me numb. By presenting the tragic deaths of people, biodiversity and ecosystems merely through numbers, their identities, existence and the politics of power behind them are concealed.
World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing
11 Nov 2026
A woman poses for a selfie with UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) mascot Caretta in Antalya, Turkey on 11 November, 2026. Reuters
The figures presented for the 1,500 people killed in a heatwave in France, the 1,134 killed in the Rana Plaza disaster in Bangladesh, or the 500,000 killed in the Bhola cyclone force us to consider whether, after death, people or trees become nothing more than ‘numbers’.
Similarly, the deaths of one tiger and 4.1 million trees in the Sundarbans of Bangladesh during Cyclone Sidr, the loss of 2.2 million tonnes of rice during the 1998 floods, or the destruction of 4.7 hectares of forest in Brazil’s Amazon due to fire are also reduced to mere ‘mathematical figures’.
Such forms of domination cannot be justified in assessing, disclosing and presenting losses and damages. This domination has emerged from the festering wounds of unjust capital and authoritarian power. The narrative of the climate platform must be freed from these wounds of injustice, and justice must be established. At the same time, state parties must build climate governance frameworks that are inclusive, equitable, diversity-friendly and people-centred.
UNFCCC COP31: Zero waste, food security and resilient cities for Bangladesh
10 Nov 2026
Those who have died—people, birds, tigers, trees and wildlife—are not merely physical entities; they are historical witnesses to a vast world of living memories. There is no initiative on the climate platform to decipher these memory imprints of living beings. As a result, losses such as death or the destruction caused by the collapse of a bridge are invariably considered ‘economic’ and measured solely in monetary terms. Although the narrative of ‘non-economic losses and damages’ has been incorporated into the climate framework, its significance remains smaller than a mustard seed.
Will trees remain deprived of the freedom to live?
On the occasion of Turkiye’s National Afforestation Day, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres opened the Leaders’ Summit on its third day by planting olive saplings. Seeing the tree-planting photograph in the media reminded me of the lost relatives of these olive saplings—the trees brutally killed in Palestine because of war.

Published: 13 Nov 2026, 03: 28
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home from Turkiye after attending COP31. 13 November 2026. BSS
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home Friday morning after concluding his three-day official visit to Turkiye, where he attended the COP31 World Leaders’ Summit and held a series of bilateral meetings with world leaders.
“A Turkish Airlines flight carrying the prime minister, his wife Zubaida Rahman and members of his entourage landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at around 5:40 am,” said Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman.
The flight left Istanbul airport around 8:00 pm Istanbul time on Thursday. The prime minister had earlier flown to Istanbul from Antalya, landing at Istanbul Airport at 6:30 pm.
The premier departed Antalya at 4:30 pm, where Ambassador Subutay Yuksel, a senior official of Türkiye’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, saw him off at the airport.

Planning and Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni, Dhaka North City BNP Member Secretary SM Jahangir Hossain, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani and PM's principal secretary ABM Abdus Sattar welcomed him at the airport.
The prime minister arrived in Antalya on 10 November on a three-day visit to attend COP31 World Leaders' Summit. On Thursday, he addressed the High-Level Segment of COP31, outlining five urgent actions to address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries.
On the sidelines of the summit, he held bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and UK Foreign Secretary Edward Miliband.
The prime minister also paid courtesy calls on the presidents of Brazil, the Maldives, Iran, Syria and Somalia, and the prime ministers of Moldova, Pakistan and Kuwait. He also met the Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Mayor of London and representatives of international organisations.

In his meeting with Erdogan, discussions covered political relations, mutual cooperation and international issues, including Bangladesh’s possible role in promoting peace in the Muslim world. The prime minister highlighted Bangladesh’s long experience and contribution to UN peacekeeping.
With Albanese, he sought Australia’s cooperation in expanding investment in Bangladesh and in ensuring the safe repatriation of Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh to their homeland in Myanmar.
In talks with Han Zheng, the two sides discussed strengthening political and economic relations, with emphasis on Chinese investment in energy, heavy industries, infrastructure and employment generation.
Meeting Miliband, the prime minister sought greater British diplomatic engagement to ensure the safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation of Rohingyas to Myanmar. They also discussed Bangladesh’s climate adaptation efforts, migration and ways to strengthen bilateral economic ties.
With Mirziyoyev, Tarique Rahman discussed establishing direct air connectivity, easing visa procedures and expanding bilateral cooperation. The Uzbek president invited him to visit Uzbekistan, and the prime minister expressed hope of making the visit in the new year.
The leaders congratulated him on Bangladesh’s democratic transition and his electoral mandate and expressed interest in strengthening bilateral ties.
